errors.english: and its cause does not turn into darkness
errors.why: The Tibetan says the lamp does not on that account become red (the rakta 'red/attached' pun that the next line resolves as 'not going into attachment'); there is no 'darkness' and རྒྱུ་ཅན means 'on account of it', not 'its cause'.

fix.find: and its cause does not turn into darkness
fix.replace: and it does not on that account turn red

note: A close and readable rendering of the Buddha's verses to the ascetic; only the lamp simile misses the red/attachment wordplay.

errors.english: is the characteristic of the action, the subsequent moments of mind
errors.why: ལས་ here is the grammatical karman (object/patient) contrasted with the agent (བྱེད་པ་པོ), so 'having been sought' is a property of the object, not of 'the action'.

errors.english: great compassion—which desires to be free from previous suffering
errors.why: སྔར་གྱི qualifies the great compassion described earlier as the wish [for beings] to be free from suffering; it is not 'previous suffering'.

note: Sound rendering of the cittotpāda definition and the eight abhisamayas; two small misreadings in the grammatical analysis.

errors.english: If one hears someone inside, one should wait.
errors.why: The root says that, when [the sound] is heard, the one who has gone in also [makes a sound]; there is no instruction to wait (the commentary sentence that follows is translated correctly).

errors.english: Do not place items near the area other than those necessary for the task.
errors.why: The rule is that one should not stay/linger near it for purposes other than those connected with it, as the following commentary (not standing idly) shows; it is not about placing items.

note: Faithful practical rendering of the latrine rules with two root-text clauses slightly misconstrued.

errors.english: Thus what is remembered is non-different from what is to be proven
errors.why: དྲན་བྱ here means 'it should be recalled thus': because [the reason] is non-different from the probandum it cannot be stated; it is not 'what is remembered'.

note: A careful handling of a difficult Alaṃkāra passage; the dialectical structure and verses are kept.
Faithful translation of the prediction to the nāga king and the verses on misusing Saṅgha property.

errors.english: Because there is no incompatible factor for the mind
errors.why: The verse means the absence of an incompatible (state of) mind, as the commentary below says (སེམས་མི་མཐུན་པ་མེད་པ་དང་ཡོད་པས), not that the mind has no incompatible factor.

note: Sound rendering of the argument against the body as cause of mind; one verse line slightly misconstrued.

errors.english: having arrived at that city while wandering through the countryside
errors.why: The Tibetan (and Sanskrit sukṛtaiḥ) says the Buddha came to the city drawn by the good deeds of its people (དེ་དག་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་ལེགས་བྱས་ཀྱིས), which is dropped.

errors.english: ma bsdoms, meaning "unrestrained" or "undisciplined" in a literal sense
errors.why: The name renders Sanskrit Anaṅgaṇa 'without blemish, spotless'; glossing it as 'undisciplined' misleads.

note: Good reading of the Tibetan verses of this bilingual side; the opening merit clause is lost and the name gloss is off.

errors.english: because of the flaw that form and the others are perceived by different sense organs
errors.why: The absurd consequence is that form and the rest would be grasped by a single sense faculty (དབང་པོ་གཅིག), not by different ones.

fix.find: because of the flaw that form and the others are perceived by different sense organs
fix.replace: because of the flaw that form and the others would be perceived by a single sense organ

errors.english: one should understand that the inherent nature of the elements as a cause has also been refuted
errors.why: The Tibetan says that by this their (passion etc.) being properties of the elements has been refuted; ཆོས་ཉིད here is 'being a property', and nothing about a cause is said.

fix.find: one should understand that the inherent nature of the elements as a cause has also been refuted
fix.replace: one should understand that their being properties of the elements has also been refuted

errors.english: the (wind) rlung, one of the primary bodily humors and the other elements
errors.why: Wind etc. are here the humors (doṣa), which the argument distinguishes from the elements (bhūta); calling them 'the other elements' blurs the step the passage makes.

errors.english: It is not logical to follow the five sense sources, such as form, as being merely the elements themselves
errors.why: The sentence says it is not right for the mere elements to be present in (follow) the five āyatanas such as form; the English inverts subject and object into an unclear sentence.

note: The anti-materialist argument is followed in outline, but the key reductio about a single sense organ is reversed and the opening step is misrendered.
Faithful rendering of the commentary on manifestation, inference of sense operation and yogic perception.
Accurate translation of the Vigrahavyāvartanī passage on the establishment of pramāṇas and infinite regress, verses kept as verse.
